outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Challenges in Efficient LLM Fine-tuning
outline.description: This chapter introduces why fine-tuning large language models improves their capabilities, explains the prohibitive memory requirements of full precision training especially for models larger than ten billion parameters, reviews prior attempts at low-bit inference that fail during backpropagation, and formulates the central problem that QLoRA aims to solve.
subtopics: The role of instruction fine-tuning in enhancing model performance
Memory consumption of conventional BF16/FP16 fine-tuning (e.g., >780 GB for LLaMA‑65B)
Why existing post-training quantisation methods break during gradient computation
Parameter-efficient approaches such as LoRA that keep most weights frozen
The objective of achieving full BF16 performance while fitting training on a single GPU

outline.description: This chapter covers the mathematical foundations behind reducing numeric precision in neural networks, focusing on blockwise k-bit quantisation methods that are widely used for large language models.
subtopics: Definition of quantisation and dequantisation operations
Uniform scaling versus non-uniform scaling strategies
"Blockwise" or "groupwise" quantisation to mitigate outlier effects
Common low-bit data types used in practice (Int8, Int4, Float8/FP8)
Error metrics introduced by compression (quantisation noise, overflow)
Information-theoretic perspective: entropy maximisation via equal bin populations

outline.description: This chapter explains Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), its mathematical formulation, how gradients flow through frozen pretrained weights into small trainable matrices, and its memory characteristics.
